page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.se1.2xlarge is an x86_64 architecture server instance within the ecs.se1 family, utilizing the KVM hypervisor. It is configured with 8 dedicated physical cores powered by an Intel Xeon 8163 processor operating at a base frequency of 2.5 GHz. The instance features 64.0 GB of system memory, yielding a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core. It does not include local storage or integrated GPU hardware, and it provides a baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps.

Benchmark evaluations indicate a performance profile that leans toward memory-intensive workloads rather than raw compute speed. The instance registers weak single-core and multi-core CPU performance in stress-ng and Geekbench tests, alongside poor single-threaded compression and decompression metrics. However, it demonstrates average performance in uncached large-block memory read and write bandwidth, reaching 39.75 GB/sec and 36.51 GB/sec respectively. Redis SET operations also perform at an average tier, executing 5.94 million operations per second, while static web serving throughput remains in the bottom 25%.

The primary tradeoff of the ecs.se1.2xlarge is its modest CPU compute capability relative to its substantial 64.0 GB memory capacity. This resource density makes it qualitatively cost-efficient for memory-bound applications that do not require intense CPU processing. It is suited for workloads such as caching layers, in-memory databases like Redis, and moderate database operations, but is less effective for CPU-heavy tasks like software compilation, ray tracing, or medium-to-large language model inference.
